beats.vo: At Koshiqa, we build our product with feedback from members like you.

One day, a woman from our community sent us a message that really stayed with us. She said she sees Koshiqa as her lifelong sustainable partner. But during her period days, she sometimes doesn't want to push herself to 10,000 steps. She wants to give her body some rest. And then she asked us something simple: "Can we have some rest days in the contest?" That got us thinking.
flags: Member's words — the chat text is drafted from the voiceover, not her real message. Please send her actual words and confirm she's happy for them to be shown. Her name and photo are not shown.

beats.vo: That's one of the reasons we built the Rest Card.
It finds your lowest eligible step day in the contest and automatically lifts it to 10,000 steps.
flags: “Lowest eligible day” — what makes a day eligible? The card screen says “Best used when your lowest day is under 7,500 steps”. The VO doesn't define it; fine as is unless you want a rule on screen.

beats.vo: Let's say your lowest day had 4,200 steps. Your Rest Card can add 5,800 steps, bringing that day up to 10,000.
That means more steps in your contest total, a lower deficit and potentially a better club placement!
flags: Club line — the screen says “You'll remain in the Urban Blackbuck club”, so “potentially a better club placement” doesn't show on this example.

beats.vo: One important thing to remember: The Rest Card makes your day count as a 10,000-step day for your contest progress. But it doesn't save your daily streak.
You still need at least 4,000 actual steps in a day to maintain your streak.
If your streak has already broken, the Rest Card won't restore it.

beats.vo: Because we believe fitness should be sustainable, not stressful. Some days you push yourself. Some days you give your body a little rest.
And we'll keep building Koshiqa with you, every step of the way.
